Existing agent methods fail to fully integrate the behaviour ofLarge Language Models (LLMs) into a unified process of reasoningand action. [13] This limitation prevents LLMs from rethinkingbased on global information with implicit information, especiallywhen they encounter errors. They can only correct their actionsbased on error messages about the current state. In attempting torevise their plans, they do not proactively acquire implicit informa-tion that was not previously considered. Instead, they simply iterateand correct errors by putting all action information and feedbackreceived into the LLM’s prompt, thereby falling into the trap of"local optima" in task performance. For example(Fig. 1A), in theReact method [42], LLMs progressively receive external feedbackand base their thinking and actions on the current information,thus initiating cycles of feedback, thinking and action. Action inthe current step is based solely on thinking about the feedback forthat step. If a problem arises at an intermediate step, such as thelack of cabin class information in the example, it will continue withthe missing information and get stuck. Voyager [33] and Reflexion[24] are two methods that can partially address these shortcomings.Voyager considers both feedback from the current environment anderror information to reconstruct the current action.
